_comment: A chain: a senior backend live-coding round, as drills. The recruiter said problem solving rather than algorithms, so each drill is a small backend component with an invariant to keep. Solve them in order, in one sitting, talking as in the interview: restate the problem, state the invariant, write the simplest solution that works, say where it breaks, fix it, test it, then say what changes at ten times the load. state = what is kept, event = what happens on a call, invariant = what must stay true. Drafted 2026-10-07 from the sources named on each node in nodes.json. The order book is two drills because the round asks for best and cancel first and matching after; settlement is three because place, settle and void are three invariants.

d292.title: Token Bucket
d292.state: per user: tokens and the time of the last refill
d292.event: refill by elapsed time times rate, cap at capacity, take one or refuse
d292.invariant: tokens never exceed capacity; a user never gets more than rate per second on average

d297.title: Hits In The Last Minute
d297.state: per user: a deque of the timestamps inside the window
d297.event: pop the front while it is out of the window, append now, return the length
d297.invariant: the deque holds exactly the hits inside the window
d297.change: per-user state is a deque of timestamps instead of two numbers; the window is kept by evicting the front

d289.title: Order Status From Events
d289.state: last seq, open qty and status per order; open total per user
d289.event: apply only when seq is greater than the last applied; add the delta to the user's total
d289.invariant: a duplicate or stale event changes nothing
d289.change: the key is an order and events change its state; a sequence number drops duplicates and stale events

d290.title: Reorder A Late Feed
d290.state: a heap of (ts, value); the watermark = max ts seen - L
d290.event: push holds, raises the watermark, releases the heap up to it; a push below the watermark is dropped
d290.change: out-of-order events are held in a heap until the watermark passes them, instead of dropped

d293.title: Cache With Expiry
d293.state: value and expiry per key; a heap of (expiry, key)
d293.event: get checks the expiry; expire pops due entries, skipping stale ones
d293.invariant: an entry is never returned at or after its expiry
d293.change: the heap holds expiries instead of timestamps, and a re-set key leaves a stale entry to skip

d296.title: Match An Order
d296.event: place takes from the other side's best level while the prices cross, then rests the remainder
d296.invariant: best price first, earliest order first at one price; a fill is at the resting price
d296.change: the heap is a heap of prices per side with a queue at each price; a loop on best and fill is the whole match

d288.title: Price Levels
d288.state: per side: a queue per price, a heap of prices, a level total; orders by id
d288.event: add rests; cancel sets the remaining quantity to 0; best drops dead heads and empty levels; fill takes from the head
d288.invariant: the top of the heap is a live level with a live head, after best
d288.change: the structure Match An Order was given: write add, cancel, best and fill yourself

d298.title: Reserve Liability
d298.state: per user: balance and reserved liability; per open order: user and liability
d298.event: place reserves the worst-case loss or refuses; cancel releases it
d298.change: per-user money instead of per-market orders: an order reserves its worst-case loss, cancel releases it

d291.title: Settle Once
d291.state: balances; the bets per market; seen event ids; winner per market
d291.event: settle pays stake * odds to the winners once
d291.invariant: a replayed event changes nothing; a market settles at most once
d291.change: dedupe by an event id in a set instead of a sequence number; the state that changes is money

d299.title: Void A Market
d299.state: balances; the bets per market; winner per settled market; seen event ids; void markets
d299.event: void returns every stake, takes back the payout if settled, once
d299.invariant: a replayed event changes nothing; a market is undone at most once
d299.change: the reverse of settle: take back the payout and return every stake, guarded the same way

d294.title: Lost Update
d294.event: debit checks the caller's version against the current one, then the funds, then writes and bumps
d294.invariant: two writers that read the same version cannot both succeed
d294.change: two callers at once on one balance; the version number is what makes the second write fail

d295.title: Most Active Users In The Last Day
d295.event: filter by a window computed from now, group by user, order by count then id
d295.invariant: a bet exactly 24 hours old counts
d295.change: the window question in SQL: the per-user count is a GROUP BY, the window is date arithmetic
